summary: Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist. Between 1842 and 1845 he studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848–1901) and the Prussian Academy of Sciences (~1857–1901).

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme (~1961–1965). He served as Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002), Director at the University of Hamburg (1990–1991), and Professor emeritus at ICPBS.
Alec M. Terrana is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Pomona College (~2010–2014), where he studied under committee members Zhiru Ng and Andrew Aisenberg.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs (~2011–2016), later holding posts at SUTD (2015–2017) and Shan State Buddhist University (~2017).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He served as a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2011–2014) and as a university assistant at the University of Vienna (~2015).
Alex McKay is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (~1990–1995) and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA), supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Wolfson College (~2005–2008), Harvard (~2011–2016), and Ashoka University (~2016).

Alex Wayman studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley (PhD under Ferdinand Diederich Lessing), and Nalanda University. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Michigan (~1960–1961), Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1966), and Columbia University (1966–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers (~1961–1965), Princeton, and Harvard (~1965–1972), and trained under traditional teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, Lodro Gyatso, Lobpon Thubten Choephel, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Alexander Coburn Soper was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College (~1921–1925) and Princeton University (~1925–1929), and held posts at Bryn Mawr College (~1939–1960) and New York University (~1960–1993).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1816–1818) and with traditional teachers Kunga Cholek Dorje and Sangye Phuntsok, later serving as sub-librarian at the Asiatic Society (~1837–1842).

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~2000–2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~2011).
Alexander James O'Neill is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held an appointment as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) as chief justice and first member of his majesty's council, and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1849).

Alexander Kabanoff was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and as head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Lubotsky is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University (~1974–1979) and Leiden University (~1980–1987), where he held a post in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a religious studies scholar who studied at SIT Graduate Institute (~2011–2013) under advisor Elizabeth Morrison.

Alexander O. Hsu works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~2010–2018) under supervisors Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University (~2017–2018).

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Moscow University (~1946–1951) and under George Roerich (~1957–1960), later holding posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–1973), Moscow State University, and SOAS (~1975–1994).

Alexander Rogers was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).
